claims.text: Electrodeposition can produce noble-metal-based HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
Electrodeposition can provide precise atomic control over the resulting HEA nanoframework.
Noble-metal ions in an electrolyte solution can serve as the initial material state for nanoframework formation.
Controlled potential and current density are operative electrodeposition parameters for producing the HEA nanoframework.
The proposed electrodeposition can be performed at room temperature and atmospheric pressure.
A specific electrolyte composition is required for the proposed electrodeposition.
The electrode substrate acts as the structural mediator in nanoframework formation.
Metal ions are reduced at the electrode surface during electrodeposition.
Reduction of metal ions at the electrode surface leads to formation of a three-dimensional HEA nanoframework.
The resulting HEA nanoframework will have a BET specific surface area of at least 100 m^2/g.
Potential, current density, and electrolyte composition bound or influence successful nanoframework production.
Substrate material and surface roughness may affect the resulting nanoframework structure.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires a surface area of at least 100 m^2/g, but the stated surface-area falsification threshold is only below 50 m^2/g. Results from 50 to below 100 m^2/g would fail the prediction without necessarily satisfying the stated falsification rule.
